title: Synthetic microburst composer log — Meera
content:
Goal:
- Build a small, repeatable synthetic microburst "composer" that mixes long-chat requests (seq len ~1200 tokens) and tiny embedding calls (~8 tokens) to stress context cache hot paths + batching.
- Compare two serving configurations: fp16 baseline vs int8/quantized kernel variant with kv-cache sharing enabled.
- Measure tail behavior (p95/p99/p999) under short spike patterns and small sustained ramps.

Testbed / config:
- Cluster: dev-gpu-pool-3 (4xA100-80GB), single replica of model endpoint per run.
- Models tested: redwood-v1 (fp16) and redwood-v1-q8 (int8).
- Runtime flags: 
  --batch-max-tokens=20480
  --batch-timeout-ms=3
  --kv-sharing=on
  --continuous-batching=on
- Client generator: python scripts/synthetic_composer.py (attached below snippet).

Arrival patterns tried:
1) Microburst: 500 concurrent tiny embedding requests arriving at t0 (10ms window) co-mingled with slowly starting 20 chat requests (stagger 100ms).
2) Sawtooth: 30s low qps (20 qps), then 10s spike (700 qps), repeat x6.
3) Poisson background + rare mega-burst: Poisson(λ=50/s) with one 2k qps pulse at t=40s.

Instrumentation:
- Collect per-request latency from client (end-to-end) and server-side per-token time.
- Export traces to local zip: /tmp/microburst-runs/<run-id>.zip
- Capture GPU utilization, nvlink traffic, and kernel invocation histograms.

Commands (abridged):
- start endpoint: ./bin/serve --model redwood-v1 --replicas 1 --config /etc/serve/dev-batch.cfg &
- run generator: PYTHONPATH=. python tools/synthetic_composer.py --pattern microburst --concurrency 600 --duration 120 --mix "emb:0.85,chat:0.15" --out run-microburst-1.json
- summarise: python tools/latency_summary.py run-microburst-1.json --percentiles 50,95,99,99.9

Key raw numbers (selected runs) — microburst pattern (single endpoint, 1 replica):
- fp16 baseline:
  * total requests: 18,600 (120s)
  * mean latency (embeddings): 12 ms
  * p95 (embeddings): 48 ms
  * p99 (embeddings): 132 ms
  * p999 (embeddings): 620 ms (heavy tail during 500-concurrent spike)
  * chat mean: 280 ms (steady) p99 chat: 1.9 s
  * GPU util: 78% avg, occasional 98% during spike (short 200ms peaks)
- q8 variant (same run):
  * total requests: 18,600 (same workload)
  * mean latency (embeddings): 10 ms
  * p95 (embeddings): 42 ms
  * p99 (embeddings): 110 ms
  * p999 (embeddings): 440 ms
  * chat mean: 300 ms (slightly up) p99 chat: 2.6 s (more variability on long sequences)
  * GPU util: 85% avg, peaks to 100% during burst (sustained ~400ms)

Observations / interpretation:
- Quantized path reduces mean and p95 for small embedding requests (better throughput), but increases p99/p999 for long-chat sequences — likely because quant kernel falls back to slower codepath for long KV updates and the GPU pipeline stalls when batch formation favors tiny requests.
- The microburst of tiny requests triggers many tiny batches which starve the long-chat token streaming (observed as chat p99 spikes).
- KV-sharing helps reduce repeated context recomputation for chat but doesn't fully mitigate pipeline contention when microburst saturates SM occupancy.
- GPU kernel launch overheads visible in nvprof logs: the q8 run shows more frequent, shorter kernel launches (more scheduling overhead).

Quick ascii micro-summary (latency buckets for embeddings, microburst run, q8):
- <10ms: 56%
- 10-50ms: 32%
- 50-200ms: 9%
- >200ms: 3% (long tails tied to concurrency spikes)

Hypothesis to validate next:
1) Introduce request shaping on the frontend: reserve soft lane capacity for long-chat (token-stream) and limit embedding lane concurrency during spikes. Expectation: reduce chat p99 without large drop in embedding throughput.
2) Increase batch-timeout-ms to 6ms for q8 path to allow slightly larger batches of tiny requests — reduces kernel launch overhead. Measure effect on embedding mean/p95 and chat tail.
3) Add per-model prioritization in router: prefer fp16 for chat-like long sequences and q8 for embeddings. Test routing policy fallback under capacity constraints.

Quick TODOs:
- [ ] Re-run microburst with batch-timeout-ms=6 on q8 and capture p999 (owner: Luca)
- [ ] Add a logging flag to record per-batch kernel type (fp16/q8) and size (owner: Meera)
- [ ] Open a small perf PR to the runtime to allow lane reservation knobs (JIRA-4321 assigned)
- [ ] Create dashboard chart: embedding lane p95 vs chat p99 across routing policies (owner: Anya)

Notes to self / gotchas:
- When reproducing, be sure to pin client clocks (NTP) otherwise p999 jitter flips around by ~50-150ms.
- On dev-gpu-pool-3 there is a noisy neighbor that sometimes kicks a process at 03:xx UTC; ignore runs shorter than 2 mins.

Attached snippets (inline):
- synthetic_composer.py generator: uses alternating poisson/tophat schedules, supports "mix" percentages per type and can pin to specific source IPs to simulate multi-tenant patterns.

End summary (working conclusion):
- Short answer: q8 yields better mean for tiny requests but worsens worst-case for long token streams unless we add request shaping + batch tuning.
- Operational lever: per-route prioritization + small increase in batch-timeout (q8) likely gives best combined economics without changing model weights.
